raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

The weight cache (`--weight-cache-mode=daemon|client`) shares preloaded weights with serving engines through zero-copy IPC, but it was gated as CUDA-alike only: the daemon rejected anything that failed `current_platform.is_cuda_alike()`, because CUDA IPC relies on torch's `_share_cuda_` handle export. Ascend has no `_share_cuda_`, but `torch_npu` registers its own multiprocessing reduction (`reduce_tensor` / `rebuild_npu_tensor`) which gives the same zero-copy handle export over the existing `ForkingPickler` framing. This PR lets the daemon/client weight-cache modes run on NPU/Ascend, with an explicit probe and graceful CPU-copy fallback when zero-copy is unavailable.

## Modifications

- `weight_cache/daemon.py` — accept NPU past the platform gate (`is_cuda_alike() or is_npu()`) in `load()`, and generalize the error message to "IPC-capable platform (CUDA, ROCm, or NPU/Ascend)". The `expandable_segments` guard is unchanged: it inspects `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF` / `PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF`, which only affect CUDA's allocator (NPU uses `PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF`).
- `weight_cache/transport.py` — add an NPU branch to `choose_daemon_transport_backend()`:
  - import `torch_npu` before the first `ForkingPickler` dump so the native NPU reducer is registered (otherwise the tensor silently falls back to a CPU copy);
  - probe `torch.multiprocessing.reductions.reduce_tensor` on one state tensor and, if it does not resolve to `rebuild_npu_tensor`, log a warning and continue with the CPU-copy path instead of failing;
  - reuse the existing `TorchIpcTransportBackend` — no dedicated NPU backend is needed, since `torch_npu` already dispatches NPU tensors natively.
- `weight_cache/ipc_loader.py` — generalize watchdog/error wording from "CUDA IPC / GPU memory" to "zero-copy IPC / device memory"; no behavior change.
- `weight_cache/protocol.py` — formatting-only cleanup; no behavior change.

Zero-copy on Ascend requires HDK >= 25.3.RC1 and CANN >= 8.3.RC1, and is unsupported on Ascend 950DT; in those cases the daemon still works via the CPU-copy fallback (with a warning). No model forward, kernel, or checkpoint layout is changed; transferred weights are byte-identical.

## Accuracy Tests
- `test_npu_weight_cache_startup.py` — Qwen3-32B, TP=2: measures cold disk load (cache off), daemon disk load, and warm client IPC import; asserts the IPC marker appears and that the warm import is faster than the cold disk load.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Loading and inference stay zero-copy; no extra data copies are introduced on the zero-copy path. The only added cost is a one-time `torch_npu` import plus a single `reduce_tensor` probe per process in `choose_daemon_transport_backend()`. The startup test above compares cold-load vs warm-IPC wall-clock and asserts the warm import is faster; per-token throughput is unaffected.

## Checklist

- [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

-        # CUDA IPC weight sharing relies on torch's _share_cuda_ handle export,

+        # (CUDA / ROCm) via _share_cuda_, and NPU via native torch_npu reduction.
+        # Fail loud here instead of dying deep inside the export with an opaque
+        # error on anything else.
+        if not current_platform.is_cuda_alike() and not is_npu():
             raise RuntimeError(
-                f"[WeightCacheDaemon] the weight cache daemon requires a CUDA-alike "
-                f"platform (CUDA or ROCm) for CUDA IPC weight sharing, but the "
-                f"active platform device type is {current_platform.device_type!r}. "
-                f"Disable the weight cache (--weight-cache-mode off)."
+                f"[WeightCacheDaemon] the weight cache daemon requires an "
+                f"IPC-capable platform (CUDA, ROCm, or NPU/Ascend) for zero-copy "
+                f"weight sharing, but the active platform device type is "
+                f"{current_platform.device_type!r}. Disable the weight cache "
+                f"(--weight-cache-mode off)."
             )
         # expandable_segments makes torch's caching allocator hand out memory
         # that cannot be exported via _share_cuda_, so the IPC export below would
         # die mid-way with an opaque CUDA error. Fail fast with an actionable
-        # message before touching the device.
+        # message before touching the device. Only CUDA's allocator is affected.
         self._assert_ipc_compatible_allocator()
         current_platform.set_device(current_platform.get_device(self.gpu_id))

@@ -184,10 +184,11 @@ def _start_daemon_liveness_watchdog(self, daemon_pid: Optional[int]) -> None:
         """Fail loud if the serving daemon dies while we hold its weights.
 
         In both client and (engine-spawned) daemon mode, the model's param.data
-        points into the daemon's GPU memory via CUDA IPC, and CUDA graphs may
-        capture those addresses. If the daemon exits, the pointers dangle:
-        forward passes would read freed GPU memory -> illegal-address crashes or
-        silent garbage. There is no safe in-place recovery, so a background
+        points into the daemon's device memory via zero-copy IPC (CUDA IPC on
+        CUDA, native torch_npu reduction on NPU), and CUDA graphs may capture
+        those addresses. If the daemon exits, the pointers dangle:
+        forward passes would read freed device memory -> illegal-address crashes
+        or silent garbage. There is no safe in-place recovery, so a background
         thread polls the daemon PID and, on death, SIGKILLs this process with a
         clear message instead of letting it serve corrupt results.
         """

                 if not _daemon_alive(daemon_pid):
                     logger.critical(
                         f"[IpcModelLoader] Weight cache daemon (pid={daemon_pid}) "
-                        f"died while this engine holds its weights via CUDA IPC. "
-                        f"The mapped weight pointers are now dangling; continuing "
-                        f"would read freed GPU memory. Terminating this process."
+                        f"died while this engine holds its weights via zero-copy "
+                        f"IPC. The mapped weight pointers are now dangling; "
+                        f"continuing would read freed device memory. Terminating "
+                        f"this process."
                     )
                     os.kill(os.getpid(), signal.SIGKILL)
                     return

@@ -190,6 +190,31 @@ def import_tensor(self, entry: Dict[str, Any]) -> torch.Tensor:
 def choose_daemon_transport_backend(
     state_tensors: Mapping[str, Tuple[torch.Tensor, bool]],
 ) -> WeightCacheTransportBackend:
+    from sglang.srt.utils.common import is_npu
+
+    if is_npu():
+        # torch_npu must be imported before the first ForkingPickler dump of an
+        # NPU tensor so its reducer is registered; otherwise the tensor falls
+        # back to a CPU copy instead of zero-copy IPC. Probe once and warn (rather
+        # than error) if zero-copy is unavailable, so weight caching still works
+        # by copying the weights through the CPU.
+        import torch.multiprocessing.reductions as _reductions
+        import torch_npu  # noqa: F401
+
+        first = next(iter(state_tensors.values()), None)
+        if first is not None:
+            rebuild_fn, _ = _reductions.reduce_tensor(first[0].data)
+            if getattr(rebuild_fn, "__name__", None) != "rebuild_npu_tensor":
+                logger.warning(
+                    "NPU weight-cache zero-copy IPC is unavailable: tensor "
+                    "reduced to %r instead of torch_npu's rebuild_npu_tensor; "
+                    "falling back to a CPU copy. Zero-copy requires Ascend HDK "
+                    ">= 25.3.RC1 and CANN >= 8.3.RC1, and is unsupported on "
+                    "Ascend 950DT.",
+                    rebuild_fn,
+                )
+        logger.info("[weight_cache] Using transport backend: %s", TORCH_IPC_BACKEND)
+        return TorchIpcTransportBackend()
     if VmmFdTransportBackend.can_export_state(state_tensors):
         logger.info("[weight_cache] Using transport backend: %s", VMM_FD_BACKEND)
         return VmmFdTransportBackend()
